# QxChat — Full Reference (llms-full.txt)

> QxChat is an open-source (MIT), end-to-end encrypted messaging platform you host on your own server. Canonical site: https://getqxchat.com/

## What is QxChat?

QxChat is built on the belief that communication tools should be transparent, self-hosted, and free from centralized telemetry. You host the server, you own the keys: every room generates its own encryption key on-device, messages are encrypted before leaving the client, and the server only routes ciphertext it mathematically cannot read. Voice and video stream via your own TURN server using WebRTC P2P. No analytics, no telemetry — just a WebSocket connection between you and a server you control.

## Key facts

- License: MIT, 100% open source (client, server, everything). No "open core".
- E2EE: client-side, on by default. Per-room keys, device signing keys (ECDSA P-256), post-quantum hybrid signatures (ML-DSA-65) and key encapsulation (ML-KEM-768) via the QXP-PHANTOM friend protocol.
- Performance: ~45 MB RAM idle (vs ~600 MB Discord), ~6 MB installer (vs ~140 MB Discord), ~0.3s cold start. No bundled Chromium (Tauri v2 + system WebView).
- Platforms: Windows (.msi, x64/ARM64), macOS (.dmg, Apple Silicon/Intel), Linux (AppImage/.deb/.rpm, x64/ARM64), Android (.apk), iOS (unsigned .ipa via sideload), NixOS (flake), plus web client at https://qxch.at/app
- Stack: Vue 3 + TypeScript (lqxp framework), Tauri v2, Rust WebSocket core (qxprotocol), WebRTC P2P media.
- Storage: messages in RAM only (150/room cap, lost on restart); SQLite/PostgreSQL for accounts and room metadata.
- Auth: password + 12-word BIP39 recovery phrase, Argon2id hashing, 7-day session tokens (SHA-256 stored).
- Source: https://github.com/lqxp — Community: https://discord.wf/qxchat — Email: contact@qxch.at

## Repositories (all MIT, under github.com/lqxp)

- lqxp/lqxp (Rust) — Server core and protocol: lightweight E2EE irc-like network, qxprotocol binary exposing HTTP API + WebSocket. Topics: e2ee-chat, messenger, protocol.
- lqxp/client (Vue) — Core QxChat client: cross-platform UI shared by the Tauri desktop/mobile apps and the hosted web client at https://qxch.at/app
- lqxp/app (Rust/Tauri v2) — Desktop and mobile apps: native binaries, releases (.msi, .dmg, AppImage, .apk, .ipa) published at https://getqxchat.com/download
- lqxp/site (Vue/Nuxt) — Official public website: landing, download and handbook at https://getqxchat.com/
- lqxp/qxchat.ts (TypeScript/Bun) — High-performance selfbot SDK for building bots on QxChat.

## Contact & Support

- Email: contact@qxch.at (general, press, partnerships, security).
- Fastest support: Discord https://discord.wf/qxchat or the default in-app room (open https://qxch.at/app or any native app).
- Bugs & contributions: GitHub Issues and Pull Requests at https://github.com/lqxp.
- Security policy: https://getqxchat.com/.well-known/security.txt

## Comparisons (as stated on getqxchat.com, Windows 11 idle, 5 encrypted rooms)

- RAM: QxChat ~45 MB vs Element ~300 MB vs Slack ~500 MB vs Discord ~600 MB.
- Installer: QxChat ~6 MB vs Discord 139 MB vs Slack 146 MB vs Element 183 MB.
- Cold launch: QxChat ~0.3s vs Element ~2.8s vs Discord ~3.5s vs Slack ~4.2s.
